channel.title: Cityside Journalism Initiative - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Cityside Journalism Initiative (berkeleyside.org)

item.title: Laura X got spousal rape banned in California. At 85, she scrapes by in a Berkeley hotel room
item.description: Born wealthy, her inheritance went to building a million-page women’s history archive — and to a Ponzi scheme. Now she relies on friends and lives in a tiny room she calls a “nun’s cell.”

item.title: East Bay loses multiple sushi spots, cafes among January restaurant closures
item.description: Sumo Sushi, Uzen, Coffee Cultures, and Delah Coffee's Berkeley location all shuttered in the first month of 2026.

item.title: 7 East Bay desserts to share with your sweetie this Valentine’s Day
item.description: Nosh shares its favorite creative, decadent desserts perfect for splitting with a special someone.

item.title: Berkeley is defying the will of voters to hold police accountable
item.description: The resignation last month of two members of the city's civilian police oversight board should alarm everyone in Berkeley.

item.title: Still no agreement between Berkeley teachers, BUSD after state mediation
item.description: As negotiations continue, hundreds of educators packed Berkeley’s school board meeting last week, asking for more pay and benefits and smaller classes. Teachers have voted to strike in San Francisco and at other districts across the state.

item.title: City Council fires head of Berkeley’s civilian police oversight office
item.description: Hansel Aguilar, the director of police accountability since 2022, has chafed against the city’s administration, drawn the ire of its council and sued its police chief over access to department records.

item.title: UC Berkeley chancellor says he’ll defend Cal from Trump by boosting research funds
item.description: Rich Lyons spoke with Berkeleyside about the state of free speech at Berkeley and what he’s doing to capture more revenue from discoveries made on campus.

item.title: New laws make heat pump installers a hot commodity
item.description: A local company called 1-888-Heat-Pumps is expanding as both Berkeley and regional rules push homeowners to adopt the new type of heating and cooling device.

item.title: Oakland’s famous tostada is back. Cenaduria Elvira is opening near Jack London Square
item.description: Her regional Mexican fare attracted national accolades and international visitors to her backyard patio. Now, Elvira Varela is ready to open her first brick-and-mortar restaurant.

item.title: BART releases doomsday scenario in case sales tax doesn’t pass
item.description: A proposal to raise $1 billion a year will likely be on the November ballot. But BART is planning for massive service cuts — including a total system shutdown — if the measure is voted down.
